interface.longDescription: Seven skills cover EasyEDA Pro control, schematic design, PCB layout, component libraries, manufacturing release, design review and extension development. The legacy batch writer remains runtime-disabled. Dispatcher ded07x99dcxb504 is connected-read-admitted only on its reviewed tuple; future mismatches fail closed. Version-pinned typed API adapters distinguish public subsets, native equivalents, blocked implementations and documented omissions. Discovery is not execution support. Current writers are limited to eligible unused project-local symbol metadata and schematic-container titles, with separate disposable symbol-copy and PCB-title workflows. Each requires current admission, original ownership, complete closed-database effect checks and fresh saved readback. Generic schematic/PCB geometry, referenced-symbol propagation and library writers remain unfinished. The one-shot String precreate workflow qualifies original PCB/project-worker sources, optionally compares common state with its original pre-open SQL inventory, and collects paired model, worker, move/startup and actor/local-clock observations. V3 retains up to 712KiB in its journal and returns compact summaries; its total budget is 215 requests, or 237 with common. Only a stored-comparison refusal after successful cleanup, context checks and durable publication permits the independent precreate read. Other failures require cleanup. Sampled empty queues and compatible startup flags do not prove complete publishers, hidden receiver identity, future Save timing or contained write destinations. This update also adds dormant actor/SQL provenance, private Windows and server-time clock components, and a durable one-create/one-Save comparison ledger. These are not registered writer, Save or clock actions. The full original-owner dispatch, closed SQL, fresh reopen, final closure and visual acceptance remain unfinished. Installed073200 opened the disposable PCB and qualified source, then timed out at common presentation before precreate/create/explicit Save. Its original owner was released only after separately approved forced recovery, with unchanged disposable bytes. That recovery does not qualify normal closure or the new integration. The cooperative common-reader deadline is not a proven fix for the live timeout. Startup/opening use the existing profile and may restore tabs, migrate, replay caches or automatically Save; they are not isolated. Ambiguous calls stay consumed. Normal closure, original root/Job termination, helper release and record settlement are separate steps. No force-exit action, Save/Discard choice, blind retry, caller JavaScript or unrestricted Save is exposed. Historical journals cannot recreate ownership. Missing installation files select offline-only startup; the installed-catalog checker uses a separate synthetic profile. Consult the skills and exhaustive coverage inventory for exact supported subsets and remaining work.
